english.title: Arrest of a child / young person by a constable for breaking remand condition
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) you were arrested by a constable

(A)_[for breaking]_
(B)_[being likely to break]_

(C)_[a remand conditions, namely **(..SPECIFY THE REMAND CONDITION..),]_
(D)_[remand conditions, namely **(..SPECIFY THE REMAND CONDITIONS..),]_

being a person

(E)_[remanded]_
(F)_[committed]_

on **(..SPECIFY DATE ..) by **(..SPECIFY COURT..) to the care of **(..SPECIFY THE LOCAL AUTHORITY..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 23A of the Children and Young Persons Act 1969.

english.notes:
This CJS Code and Standard Offence Wording document is now OBSOLETE repealed as from 03/12/2012 by Schedule 12 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.

The above "wording" is NOT AN OFFENCE.

(i) This wording is supplied by PNLD for information only (some forces do prepare a 'charge form' for administrative purposes i.e. to generate an entry on the court register and to assist the court).
(ii) section 23A(2) of the Children and Young Persons Act 1969 provides that a person arrested under section 23A(1)

(a) must, except where he was arrested within 24 hours of the time at which he is to appear before the court in pursuance of the remand or committal, be brought as soon as practicable and in any event within 24 hours after his arrest before a justice of the peace; and (b) if the exception in paragraph (a) applies he must be brought before the court before which he was to have appeared.

(iii) For the purposes of section 23A(2), in reckoning any period of 24 hours, no account will be taken of Christmas Day, Good Friday or any Sunday.
(iv) Section 23A(3) of the Children and Young Persons Act 1969 provides that a Justice of the Peace before whom a person is brought under section 23A(2):-

(a) if of the opinion that that person has broken any condition imposed on him under section 23(7) or (10) must remand him; and that section applies as if he was then charged with or convicted of the offence for which he had been remanded or committed;
(b) if not of that opinion must remand him to the place to which he had been remanded or committed at the time of his arrest subject to the same conditions as those which had been imposed on him at that time.

other.powersofarrest: Section 23A(1) of the Children and Young Persons Act 1969 provides:- "A person who has been remanded or committed to local authority accommodation and in respect of whom conditions under section 23(7) a or (10) have been imposed may be arrested without warrant by a constable if the constable has reasonable grounds for suspecting that that person has broken any of those conditions.
other.penalty:
Not applicable - this is NOT AN OFFENCE

In spite of the fact that a power of arrest exists for breaching remand conditions it is NOT an offence.

Procedures whereby the case is presented at court will vary from force to force, however, some magistrates clerks demand some form of paper work to be completed which generates an entry in the court register.

Therefore to assist forces who require this procedure the above 'pseudo' standard offence wording is provided.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
